summary.headline: Earns more on shareholder money than peers, but cash flow checks weak
summary.takeaway: JPMorgan turns shareholder money and sales into profit better than similar banks. Health checks are mixed: the Piotroski score is low, and many standard debt tests do not apply to banks.

positives.text: ROE (profit made from shareholders' money) is 18%, well above the peer median of 11.1%.
Keeps about $32.50 of every $100 in revenue as profit, more than similar banks (peer median 27.8%).
Share count fell from 2.88B to 2.78B, so each remaining share owns a slightly bigger part of the company.

watch_outs.text: Piotroski score (checks of financial strength) is 3 of 7, passing fewer than half of the checks that could be measured.
Operating cash flow was -$147.78B while net profit was $57.05B, so reported profit did not show up as cash.
Equity multiplier is 13.2x (assets compared with shareholder money). ROA (profit compared with assets) is 1.37%, down slightly from 1.5%.

what_to_watch_next: Next earnings report on 14 Jan 2027: watch whether operating cash flow turns positive.
Whether ROA holds near 1.4% or keeps slipping from 1.5%.
summary.ask_yourself: How comfortable are you with a company that uses a lot of borrowed money to earn its profits?
data_gaps: Altman Z-score is not used for banks, so there is no bankruptcy-risk score.
Debt to equity, net debt, interest coverage and current ratio are not meaningful for banks.
ROIC and gross margin do not apply to banks; operating margin is missing.
Only 7 of 9 Piotroski checks could be measured.
No history comparison for ROE or net margin, only peer medians.
